lesson.title: Sectors of the whole
lesson.subtitle: P4 pie-chart revision
lesson.objective: Recognise sectors of a pie chart as a half, a quarter or an eighth of the whole, with no cuts drawn.
lesson.story: The pie chart sorts the pupils into groups: Rice, Noodles, Bread and Soup. The whole circle is 8 equal parts, but the cuts between them are not drawn.

steps.title: Name the sector
steps.prompt: What fraction of the whole pie is the Rice sector?
hints: Compare the sector with the whole circle.
Imagine the circle cut into 8 equal parts, like a pizza. How many of those parts would the sector cover?
Rice covers 4 of the 8 equal parts, and 4/8 is a half.

steps.title: Count the parts
steps.prompt: The whole circle is 8 equal parts, but the cuts are not drawn. How many of the 8 parts does the Noodles sector cover?
hints: Think about how much of the whole circle the sector fills.
Work out how many of the 8 parts make a half, a quarter or an eighth of the circle.
The Noodles sector is a quarter, and a quarter of 8 parts is 2 parts.
The Noodles sector covers 2 of the 8 parts. Enter 2.

steps.title: What a sector shows
steps.prompt: What does a sector of a pie chart show?

choices.label: How much of the whole pie the group takes up.
How many items are in the group, counted as a number.
How wide the corner of the sector is at the centre.

hints: Think about what the whole circle stands for.
Every sector is one part of that whole.
A sector tells you the fraction of the whole that one group makes up.
Choose the share of the whole.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Why can you name a sector as a half or a quarter when no cuts are drawn?

choices.label: The colour of the sector tells you which fraction of the pie it shows.
Compare it with the whole circle: a half fills half, a quarter a quarter.
The biggest sector in any pie chart is always exactly one half of it.

hints: Think about how much of the circle the sector fills.
A half is as much as the other half left over.
Compare the sector with the whole circle, not with its colour.
Choose the explanation about comparing with the whole circle.
